draft.title: Sedimentary rocks
card: Sediments are loose pieces of rock, sand, mud or shell, or the remains of living things. Water, wind or ice carry them and drop them in a new place.
Sediments settle in layers. The oldest layer is usually at the bottom, because newer layers are laid on top.

Over a very long time, new layers bury the older ones. The weight squeezes the sediments, and minerals in the water glue them together. This is called cementing, and it makes sedimentary rock, such as sandstone.
Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock. A dead animal buried in soft sediment can be kept as the sediment becomes rock.
draft.remember: Sedimentary rock is made from layers of sediment that are buried and cemented over a long time.

opts: Sand is laid down, buried and cemented into rock
Sand is melted deep underground, then cools into rock
Sand is changed by heat and pressure without melting
Sand is blown into a pile and stays as loose grains
a.why: Sandstone is sedimentary, so it forms when sand is laid down in layers, buried and cemented. Melting would make an igneous rock, and a loose pile of sand has not been buried or cemented, so it is not rock.
a.clue: Think about layers, burial and glue-like minerals.

b.q: Layers of mud settle on the floor of a lake in Tasmania. A dead fish is buried in one layer. Over millions of years the layers harden. Where is the fish fossil most likely to be found?
opts: In sedimentary rock formed from the mud
In igneous rock formed from cooled lava
In the loose mud at the surface today
In rock that was melted and then cooled
b.why: The mud was buried in layers and cemented, so it became sedimentary rock, which is where most fossils are found. Igneous rock forms from molten rock, which would destroy a fish, so it is not a likely place for a fossil.
b.clue: Which rock forms from buried layers of sediment?

a.best: Sand is laid down, buried and cemented into rock

b.best: In sedimentary rock formed from the mud

problems.detail: The clue 'Which rock forms from buried layers of sediment?' all but names the answer, since 'sediment' points straight to 'sedimentary'. A student could pick the right option without knowing the idea.
'This is called cementing' follows both the squeezing and the gluing, so students may think squeezing (compaction) is part of cementing. Cementing is only the minerals gluing the grains together.

check.summary: The facts are correct and both questions have one clear answer. The clue for question b nearly gives the answer away, and the card could make it clearer that cementing means only the mineral gluing, not the squeezing.
